content:
ashwin: heads-up — shared-gpu-pool-us-west1 is showing sustained queue lengths and per-tenant bursty occupancy. Customers are seeing 500ms+ enqueue latencies and some requests getting 429s. Looks like a few tenants are monopolizing slots.

sre-bot: [ALERT] pool=shared-gpu-pool-us-west1 qlen>250 for 6m, p95_enqueue=520ms, affected-tenants=3

maria: digging into prometheus now. initial qps heatmap shows tenant:ad-platform and tenant:video-transcode doing long TTI traces, but ad-platform has big batch sizes (seq_len spikes).

joel: can you paste the queries? thinking we might need a short-term admission-control tweak (burst tokens -> smaller) + per-tenant concurrency cap.

maria: here are the queries i ran:

```
sum by (tenant)(rate(inference_requests{pool="shared-gpu-pool-us-west1"}[1m]))
max by (tenant)(inference_queue_length{pool="shared-gpu-pool-us-west1"})
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_enqueue_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="shared-gpu-pool-us-west1"}[5m])) by (le, tenant))
```

ashwin: ad-platform has ~42% of active slots right now, while they are only 18% of reserved budget. They are getting burst tokens repeatedly.

joel: agreed — noisy neighbor. short-term: reduce burst_tokens for shared pools from 10 -> 3 and add per-tenant max_concurrency=8 for non-enterprise tenants. long-term: need fair-share scheduler (weighted DRF-ish) so small customers don't get starved.

ophelia: warning — reducing burst_tokens may increase client 429s and user-facing errors. we should send a notice to affected tenants or return Retry-After to clients with backoff guidance.

ashwin: +1. we can return structured 429 with header `X-RI-Retry-After` and metrics so client SDKs can surface it. Also enable a short canary: change only on one AZ nodepool first.

maria: i pushed a dashboard widget showing per-tenant tokens_used, concurrency, and queue_in_time. sharing link: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash/PL4Gk/shared-gpu-fairness

joel: proposed quick fix (patch):

```
# patch: admission control config
shared_pools:
  - name: shared-gpu-pool-us-west1
    burst_tokens: 3
    per_tenant_max_concurrency:
      default: 8
      enterprise: 32
    reject_policy: "retry-after"
```

ashwin: can you run this as a canary in us-west1-a with rollout 10%? If metrics look good after 10m we can roll to rest of us-west1.

maria: starting canary now. deployed config to nodepool shared-usw1-a-canary. kube apply worked.

sre-bot: [DEPLOY] admission-config applied to shared-usw1-a-canary by maria at 1750001302

ophelia: monitoring SLOs and error budget dashboards. will watch traces for increased 429s and p99 latency rise.

joel: also opened an infra ticket to consider implementing an internal token-bucket per-tenant with leak-rate tied to reserved quota. that would allow enterprise customers to burst more while preserving fairness: TICKET-1428.

maria: first 5m of canary: overall qlen dropped 18%, ad-platform concurrency dropped from 240 -> 110, p95_enqueue down 290ms -> 145ms for non-enterprise tenants. ad-platform saw a 1.8x increase in 429s from its clients but retries look successful.

ashwin: good signals. keep canary for another 10m, notify ad-platform Slack contact to expect transient 429s. ops-runbook step: if user error >15% for 30m revert.

ophelia: notified account team. sending note: "We're throttling burst capacity in shared pools to reduce cross-tenant latency; we recommend upgrading to Dedicated for bursty workloads."

joel: longer term items we should track:
- implement weighted fair-share allocator (DRF variant) in serving runtime
- per-tenant priority classes + preemption for low-cost jobs
- automated promotion to dedicated based on sustained burst ratio
- billing signal to nudge noisy tenants (showing estimated extra GPU minutes)

maria: adding these to infra backlog and linking TICKET-1428 -> EPIC-FAIRNESS.

sre-bot: [RESOLVED] pool=shared-gpu-pool-us-west1 qlen normalized at 1750001458 (canary success).

ashwin: nice work team. follow-ups: joel please spec the DRF proposal with API impacts; ophelia coordinate account comms; maria put an automated alert to detect tenant burst imbalance (e.g., >30% of active slots for >5m).

joel: on it. i'll draft the proposal and include perf/complexity tradeoffs.

ophelia: i'll prepare a template message for affected tenants and a KB entry about "Why am I seeing 429s in shared pools".

ashwin: closing thread once the EPIC is created. thanks all.
